name: Apollo 11 EASEP

site.name: Mare Tranquillitatis (Tranquility Base)
site.description: Deployed south of the Apollo 11 Lunar Module Eagle descent stage on the basaltic plain of Mare Tranquillitatis.

endCause: The Passive Seismic Experiment Package (PSEP) command receiver stopped responding at 04:00 UTC on August 25, 1969 due to overheating during lunar midday.
scientificValue: Deployed during the first human lunar landing, the Early Apollo Scientific Experiments Package (EASEP) established the first seismic and laser-ranging outpost on the Moon. Its telemetry captured the Moon's distinct seismic scattering behavior, while its passive Laser Ranging Retroreflector remains measurable from Earth decades later.

legacy.finding: Recorded the first extraterrestrial seismic telemetry via the Passive Seismic Experiment Package across three weeks of surface operation.
legacy.sourceTitle: NASA NSSDCA Master Catalog — Apollo 11 EASEP (1969-059C)

legacy.finding: Measured surface dust and thermal cycling effects on solar-powered electronics using the Lunar Dust Detector.
Emplaced the 100-prism Laser Ranging Retroreflector (LRRR), enabling ongoing Earth–Moon distance measurements down to millimeter precision.

sources.title: NASA NSSDCA Master Catalog — Apollo 11 EASEP / LM (1969-059C)

image.alt: Monochrome technical schematic of the Apollo 11 EASEP surface instruments showing the Passive Seismic Experiment Package with twin solar panels alongside the angled Laser Ranging Retroreflector array.
